title: Multisystem Inflammatory Syndrome in Children Unmasking Brugada Type 1 Pattern
case_prompt:
A 14-year-old previously healthy Caucasian boy was admitted with a 5-day history of fever, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea. On the day of admission, he developed a diffuse skin rash and bilateral conjunctivitis. He had no personal or family history of cardiovascular disease. On examination, temperature was 38.3 °C, blood pressure was low, heart rate 112 beats/min, and oxygen saturation 96% on room air. 

Laboratory studies showed elevated N-terminal pro–brain natriuretic peptide, troponin, C-reactive protein, procalcitonin, D-dimer, fibrinogen, and hyponatremia. A SARS-CoV-2 nasopharyngeal swab was negative, but anti–SARS-CoV-2 IgG was positive. Transthoracic echocardiography demonstrated biventricular dilatation, global hypokinesia, and an ejection fraction of 30%. 

Electrocardiography in standard leads showed sinus rhythm, normal ventricular conduction, and diffuse repolarization abnormalities. Modified precordial-lead ECG revealed sinus rhythm with QRS fragmentation in lead D3 and saddleback ST-segment elevation.
diagnostic_reasoning:
1. Brugada phenocopy was initially favored due to the inflammatory state and lack of family history — “a Brugada phenocopy (BP) was suspected, given the underlying inflammatory status during hospitalization and the negative family and medical histories.”  
2. Myocarditis was considered as a cause of Brugada-like changes — “Piazza et al described a 5-year-old patient whose Brugada-like pattern was considered secondary to myocarditis without further investigations.”  
3. Autonomic imbalance was recognized as a potential trigger for transient repolarization changes — “The transient ECG pattern could have been related to an inflammatory state causing myocardial damage or to autonomic imbalance that could have altered myocardial repolarization.”  
4. Direct SARS-CoV-2–induced electrical remodeling was proposed based on prior reports of COVID-19 myocardium effects — “several case reports describe new onset of coved ST-segment elevation in right precordial leads in patients hospitalized for coronavirus disease 2019 so far, even in the absence of fever, giving rise to the hypothesis that SARS-CoV-2 itself may provoke electric remodeling…”  
5. True Brugada syndrome was confirmed by a positive sodium channel–blocker challenge — “To discriminate between Brugada syndrome (BrS) and BP, the patient was referred to an electrophysiology center…Five minutes after intravenous infusion of ajmaline 1 mg/kg, a Brugada pattern appeared.”
